facts.statement: Borealosaurus was described by Hailu, Qiang, Lamanna, Jinglu, and Yinxiang in 2004.
facts.quote: It was described by Hailu, Qiang, Lamanna, Jinglu and Yinxiang, in 2004.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was discovered in the Sunjiawan Formation in Liaoning province, China.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por Hailu, Qiang, Lamanna, Jinglu y Yinxiang, en 2004 y descubierto en la Formación Sunjiawan en la provincia de Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Borealosaurus was approximately 12 meters long, 4 meters high, and weighed an estimated 10 tonnes.
facts.quote: Borealosaurus medía aproximadamente 12 metros de largo y 4 de alto, con un peso estimado de 10 toneladas.

facts.statement: Borealosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in northern China.
facts.quote: Borealosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of northern China.

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 89 to 84 million years ago during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 89 y 84 millones de años, en el Santoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Borealosaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
The genus belongs to the subfamily Opisthocoelicaudiinae.
Borealosaurus is distinguished from other sauropods by its mid-distal caudal vertebrae featuring opistocoelous centra.
facts.quote: Borealosaurus se distingue de otros saurópodos por sus vértebras caudales mediodistales con opistocelos.

facts.statement: Researchers Averianov and Sues debated the classification, considering Borealosaurus a non-lithostrotian titanosaur because of the lack of procoely in its middle caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: However, in their overview of Cretaceous sauropod remains from Central Asia, Averianov and Sues considered Borealosaurus a non-lithostrotian titanosaur due to the lack of procoely in the middle caudal vertebrae.

rejected.statement: The specific name honors Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman, who named the first Chinese dinosaur.
rejected.quote: It was named from Greek (the North wind) and σαυρος (lizard), with its specific name being given in honor of Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman, who named the first Chinese dinosaur.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman who named the first'
